t: An Ionian Greek port near the mouth of the Cayster, founded by tradition c. 1000 BCE and famed for its sanctuary of Artemis.
The Artemision acted as bank, refuge and pilgrimage centre; its rebuilt temple was one of the Seven Wonders of the Ancient World.
Ephesus passed from Lydian, Persian, Athenian and Hellenistic overlords to Rome in 133 BCE and became the chief city of Roman Asia.
dyk: A deposit beneath the Temple of Artemis contained some of the oldest coins ever found, small lumps of electrum from around 600 BCE.
ev: Ionian settlers, by tradition led by Androclus, found Greek Ephesus
Croesus of Lydia takes the city and pays for columns of the marble Artemision
Ephesus passes under the Achaemenid Empire after the fall of Lydia
Lysander defeats the Athenian fleet at Notium, near Ephesus
Herostratus burns the Temple of Artemis
Alexander the Great restores democracy and gives the Persian tribute to Artemis
Lysimachus moves the city to a new site and renames it Arsinoeia
Attalus III bequeaths Pergamon, including Ephesus, to Rome

f.capital: Ephesus; refounded on a new site by Lysimachus c. 290 BCE
f.predecessor: Carian and Lelegian settlement (probably Bronze Age Apasa)
